response.title: Can I leave a power station in my unheated camper over the winter, or will the cold ruin it?
response.answer:
Yes, you can generally leave a portable power station in an unheated camper over winter. Cold temperatures usually won't permanently damage the battery, but there are a few important precautions.

The biggest concern is charging the battery when it's below freezing, not simply storing it in the cold.

How cold is too cold?

Most modern power stations use lithium-ion batteries, particularly LiFePO4 (LFP).

Temperature

	

What happens




32°F to 50°F (0–10°C)

	

Generally safe for storage




0°F to 32°F (−18–0°C)

	

Usually safe for storage, but don't charge below 32°F unless the manufacturer allows it




−4°F to 0°F (−20 to −18°C)

	

Often within storage limits, depending on model




Below −4°F (−20°C)

	

May exceed the manufacturer's storage rating

These are general guidelines. Some power stations have different temperature limits.

Five tips for winter storage

Charge it to around 50–60% before storing it. Avoid leaving it at 0% or 100% for months.

Turn it completely off. Disable standby modes and disconnect all devices to minimize battery drain.

Don't charge it while frozen. Charging lithium batteries below 32°F (0°C) can cause permanent damage unless the system is specifically designed to handle it.

Keep it dry. Condensation and moisture can damage the electronics, particularly when temperatures fluctuate.

Check the charge periodically. Every 1–3 months is reasonable, depending on the manufacturer's recommendations and the unit's standby drain.

What about using it during winter?

Many power stations can discharge electricity below freezing, although their available capacity and power output may decrease.

If you bring a freezing-cold power station indoors, allow it to warm above the manufacturer's minimum charging temperature before plugging it in. Also allow any condensation to evaporate.

My recommendation

If your camper experiences occasional temperatures around 10–30°F, I'd generally be comfortable leaving an LFP power station there, provided it's powered off and stored properly.

If temperatures regularly fall below 0°F, I'd lean toward bringing it indoors, especially for extended storage.

Two questions:

What brand and model is your power station? (EcoFlow, Jackery, Bluetti, Anker, etc.)

How cold does your camper get in winter? (Around 20°F, 0°F, or below?)

With those details, I can tell you whether it's safe to leave your specific power station in the camper all winter.
